why: 82 of 85 judge replies came back with the WHY line cut mid-phrase while the LABEL line survived. This probe re-ran ONE judge input at two output budgets to find out why.

runs.label: DIFFERENT
runs.text:
LABEL: DIFFERENT
WHY: The REAL answer

runs.label: UNCLEAR
runs.text:
LABEL: UNCLEAR
WHY: The REAL answer commits to the position that Syrian nationalists "would find it very, very, very difficult to sign up with ISIS," while the CANDIDATE answer takes

finding: gemini-3.5-flash charges hidden thinking against max_output_tokens and did not finish thinking at either budget: 243/256 then 980/1024 tokens went to thoughts, both runs ended MAX_TOKENS. The visible reply is whatever fits in the remainder, which is why LABEL survives and WHY does not.
material_consequence: The LABEL FLIPPED between the two budgets at temperature 0 (DIFFERENT -> UNCLEAR). The 85 labels in judgements.jsonl are therefore a function of the truncation, not only of the rubric. They are not trustworthy as scored data.
not_fixed_here: Raising the budget alone does not fix it (1024 still hit MAX_TOKENS). The fix is an explicit thinking setting on the shared GeminiClient path -- the same class of change src/doppler/gemini.py already documents for flash-lite. That changes the judge's behaviour, so it is an owner decision, not an implementer's. No re-run was made.
unaffected: The gemini-3.5-flash-lite GENERATIONS are unaffected: max tokens_out was 188 against a 256 budget, no truncation flags, and every reply ends on a complete sentence.
